## Is the Tree in the Geometry?
*Chomsky's phrase-structure trees, looked for inside trained models: subject-verb agreement across intervening clauses (2016), agreement in nonsense sentences, "colorless green" networks (2018), and the structural probe (2019), which finds parse-tree distance as squared distance in a linear subspace of BERT and tree depth as a squared norm. Against it, the theoretical limits of self-attention on unbounded bracket nesting and the positive result for bounded depth. Brackets are the right test because of the Chomsky–Schützenberger theorem (1963): every context-free language is built from balanced brackets (a Dyck language) and a regular language. Bounded depth is Chomsky's competence versus performance (1963–1965): people also parse only a few levels of centre-embedding, and a network with finite precision and context is, strictly, a large finite automaton.*

## Sparse Autoencoders and Dictionary Learning
*An autoencoder (@sec-ch-embedding-spaces) with a sparse code wider than its input, recovering more features than dimensions, which uses the near-orthogonality of @sec-ch-curse-of-dimensionality.*

## Reasoning in Text or in the Space
*Chain of thought [@wei2022chain] as a path through the model's space that is rounded to a token at every step, which puts reasoning on Shannon's boundary (@sec-ch-symbols-without-interior); pause tokens (2023) [@goyal2023think] and filler tokens (2024) [@pfau2024lets] as extra computation that is not quite language; and the latent alternatives that keep the steps in the space, continuous chain of thought (Coconut, 2024) [@hao2024training] and recurrent-depth models (2025). Planning in latent space is taken up in @sec-ch-multimodal-embeddings.*

*A path is not a geodesic. A sampled chain is one draw from a distribution over paths, and nothing guarantees that a single draw converges on the answer. What training raises is the probability $p_x$ that a draw ends in the set of answers a verifier accepts, summed over every path that does. The picture is old: problem solving as search in a problem space [@simon1971human; @newell1972human], which has guarantees only when the structure supplies them (A\* [@hart1968formal], UCT [@kocsis2006bandit]). A language model samples instead of searching, and gives up the guarantee. The same sum is the marginal likelihood of a latent-variable model whose latent variable is the chain of thought [@phan2023training], and self-consistency marginalizes it by voting [@wang2022self].*

*How the probability is raised, at inference and at training. At inference, repeated sampling raises coverage log-linearly over orders of magnitude [@brown2024large], but only an oracle verifier turns coverage into accuracy: majority voting and reward models saturate [@brown2024large, p. 10], and a learned verifier can get worse as the search finds adversarial solutions that fool it [@cobbe2021training, p. 10]. At training, REINFORCE [@williams1992simple] with a binary reward is, up to a factor, a step of fine-tuning on the model's own successful samples, the expectation-maximization reading of Dayan and Hinton [@dayan1997using]; ReST-EM is that loop and STaR approximates it [@singh2023beyond; @zelikman2022star], while group-normalized variants such as GRPO change the weighting [@shao2024deepseekmath]. The search is paid for once and amortized into the weights, as in expert iteration and AlphaZero [@anthony2017thinking; @silver2017mastering], and train-time and test-time compute can be traded [@jones2021scaling]. Whether training discovers new paths is contested: pass@k at large $k$ suggests that it reweights paths the base model already had and can lose coverage [@yue2025does], while self-training reports gains that transfer to held-out benchmarks [@singh2023beyond].*

*Why length is not the whole story. More tokens add serial computation that a fixed-depth transformer lacks [@feng2023towards; @merrill2023expressive], and test-time compute can stand in for pretraining on easy and medium questions but not on hard ones [@snell2024scaling]. Yet forcing a chain to run longer eventually stops helping [@muennighoff2025s1] and can hurt, in part because length tracks distraction [@gema2025inverse], and on easy problems it mostly wastes tokens [@chen2024do]. Search at inference and amortization in training are both real; neither alone explains the gain.*

*What the tokens mean. An outcome reward does not constrain the text. Chains are plausible yet can be unfaithful [@turpin2023language], faithfulness varies by task and falls with model size on most tasks [@lanham2023measuring], and scaling outcome-based RL leaves it on a low plateau [@chen2025reasoning]. Rounding to a token is therefore no guarantee that the token carries the step. Reward hacking is the same Goodhart effect seen from the other side: proxy rewards are rarely unhackable [@skalse2022defining], and optimizing harder hurts the true reward [@gao2022scaling]. Whether a continuous chain escapes this, and how one is trained when there is no sampled token to reward, is open.*

## Do Different Models Share a Geometry?
*Claims of representational convergence across models, as a bridge to Chapters [-@sec-ch-cross-domain-transfer] and [-@sec-ch-multimodal-embeddings], which take up alignment between spaces and across modalities.*

## Scale Test
*Here the geometry is learned rather than designed. Which of the structures of Chapters [-@sec-ch-tangent-spaces-geodesics] to [-@sec-ch-cross-domain-transfer] do trained transformers discover on their own? For reasoning, the bitter lesson [@sutton2019bitter] poses the question sharply: search and learning are the methods that scaled, so is keeping the steps in the space a prior that sampling, verification, and amortization absorb, or a different use of compute (serial depth, a distribution over paths held in one vector)? The test: at matched compute, does a latent chain beat sampled token chains plus a verifier, on problems with an oracle verifier and on problems without one?*
